title: Ostrobothnia: 1.1 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €47,900 a year
markdown:
# Ostrobothnia: 1.1 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €47,900 a year

> 1.1 more patients a year treated to cure · €47,900 of €1M · €952,100 left: nothing more pays off on today's evidence

## The gap

Of 100 lung cancer patients in Ostrobothnia, 28 get treatment that aims to cure. In Finland it is 27. The difference is within what chance alone gives a county of this size. [^care_curative] Compared with the best quarter of counties (30.4%), about 2.3 patients a year are missing from treatment that aims to cure, with a range of 0.0 to 6.0 [^model]. Against Finland as a whole there is no shortfall to split [^model]. 15.4% are operated, against 15.0% nationally [^care_surgery].

## The target

Raise the share of lung cancer patients treated to cure from 27.8% to 29.0% by 2028: 1.1 more patients a year (range 0.0–1.1), for €47,900 a year, about €45,189 per extra patient. [^care_curative][^model]

## Funded actions

| # | Action and owner | Cost a year | More patients treated to cure a year (range) | First step this week | Measure: today → target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | **The county can start on Monday** | | | | |
| 1 | **Precise radiotherapy (SBRT) for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated**[^ev_sbrt_pathway_1]. Chief physician of oncology; chief of radiotherapy at the university hospital | €19,960 | 0.7 (0.0–0.9) | Write the referral rule: every stage I patient not accepted for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy the same week. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 27.8% → 28.6% by 2028 |
| 2 | **Travel and hotel paid for patients far from the university hospital**[^ev_travel_accommodation_support_1]. Chief physician of oncology and hospital social work; university hospital patient hotel | €27,940 | 0.4 (0.0–0.3) | Name one contact person who books the patient hotel and transport for every patient sent to the university hospital for curative treatment. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 27.8% → 28.2% by 2028 |
| | **Total** | **€47,900** | **1.1 (0.0–1.1)** | | |

No trial has measured these effects; the low end of every range is zero. The ranges do not add up to the range of the total, because the measures share one ceiling. Costs are assumptions. [^model]

## Needs a national decision (outside this budget)

- **Low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers**[^ev_ldct_screening_1]: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health and Palko (decision), Finnish Cancer Registry (steering), county (delivery). €558,665 a year; modelled to avoid 1.0 deaths a year (0.2–2.5). Not counted in this budget. Not a county decision. Ask the Ministry and Palko for the timetable after the 2026-2028 pilot and offer the county as a pilot site. [^model]

## What to measure from Monday

- Share of patients treated to cure: 27.8% (2019–2023, measured) → 29.0% by 2028. [^care_curative][^model]
- The registry's public figures cover 2019–2023; count these each month from the county's own records. [^care_curative]

## What more money buys, and what it cannot

The remaining €952,100 buys nothing more in the model [^model]. The measures that add patients treated to cure are limited by the reachable part of the measured shortfall, not by money [^model]. To see what else the money could do, look at low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers, which needs a national decision, or rank measures by deaths avoided instead [^model]. About 70 people die of lung cancer a year in Ostrobothnia [^deaths]. This plan is modelled to avoid 0.2 of those deaths a year [^model].

## Pilot ask

A six-month pilot of two actions: a chest surgeon reviews every decision not to operate, and every patient who cannot be operated is referred for precise radiotherapy. In six months that is about 45 new patients and 38 decisions reviewed. If our assumptions hold, about 0 of them (0 to 1) move to treatment that aims to cure in that time, and the share rises from 27.8% to 28.9% by 2028. The pilot replaces those assumptions with a count. [^model]

## Limits

- Effects are given as ranges, not probabilities. Each range runs from lowest to highest result when every assumed effect moves together from its low to its high bound [^model].
- Shares are adjusted only for residents' age. They are not adjusted for stage, other illness, histology, how cancer was found, smoking or recording, and county figures cannot show cause [^model].
- A check found that 0 of 3 measured outcomes matched the estimated symptom-to-treatment clock beyond chance [^model].

pilot.cannot_show_en: Six months is too short to show the county's share moving. It is long enough to count reviews done, decisions changed and referrals made, against the same six months a year earlier.
